text: This is a SAMPLE marine oxygen analyzer manual created for a public RAG demo. It does not contain any confidential vendor document. The analyzer measures oxygen concentration in inert gas systems and displays the reading on the front panel.

The oxygen sensor is a consumable part. It must be replaced when its service life is exceeded or when the reading cannot be calibrated. The maximum service life of the sensor is about 2 years under normal operating conditions.

To replace the sensor, turn off the analyzer, disconnect the sensor cable, unscrew the old sensor from the sensor housing, install the new sensor, then reconnect the cable and run a calibration before returning the unit to service.

Calibration uses a span gas of known oxygen concentration. Select the Calibration menu, enter the span gas value printed on the cylinder, apply the gas until the reading is stable, and confirm to store the new span point.

Zero calibration should be performed with a nitrogen gas that contains no oxygen. Apply the zero gas until the reading settles near zero, then confirm. Do not perform zero calibration with ambient air, because air contains about 21 percent oxygen.

The storage temperature range for the analyzer and spare sensors is -15 to 55 degrees Celsius. Storing consumable parts outside this range shortens their service life and may cause inaccurate readings after installation.

The recommended operating temperature range is 0 to 45 degrees Celsius with non-condensing humidity. Keep the sample line free of moisture and dust, because contamination on the sensor face causes a slow response and drift.

Two oxygen alarm setpoints are available: a high alarm and a low alarm. Enter the Alarm menu to set each threshold as a percentage of oxygen. The relay output activates when the measured value crosses the configured setpoint.

For installation, follow the Analyzer Installation and Connections section. Mount the unit away from direct heat, connect the sample gas inlet and the power supply, and verify the flow rate is within the specified range before power-on.
Advanced settings are protected. To change them, open the Tools menu, select Service, and log in with Password level 1. Changes to alarm thresholds and calibration points require this service access.

Perform a monthly visual check of the sample line, filter, and sensor. Replace the inline filter when it is discolored. Record each calibration in the maintenance log so that sensor drift over time can be reviewed.

Calibration gases are stored under pressure. Secure all cylinders, use a proper regulator, and ventilate the space. Final decisions on maintenance and operation remain with the licensed engineer, who should verify against the original manual.
